correctness.summary: The root-relative Newton error is exactly 1-gamma*a/d, with root-secant slope a and current derivative d both in [m,L]. Endpoint maximization gives the exact envelope; continuous boundary-layer profiles prove sharpness. Equioscillation gives the optimal constant damping. The kappa=2 strict-decrease argument and kappa>2 explicit continuous-derivative two-cycle close the sharp global boundary. The derivative-aware minimax result reduces pointwise to the classical two-endpoint scalar minimax problem.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: General Newton, relaxation and Kantorovich convergence theory is prior work, and Heid's more general operator theorem already implies the sufficient strict damping condition gamma<2m/L in this scalar setting; that inequality is excluded from the novelty claim. No checked source states the full exact one-step envelope, sharp boundary behavior and two-cycle, optimal constant factor, or the derivative-aware minimax collapse. Older scalar relaxed-Newton and nonlinear-equation literature remains the main historical-equivalence risk.

value.summary: The result converts a qualitative globalization issue into an exact robustness frontier, identifies the sharp undamped conditioning threshold, gives an explicit failure mechanism just beyond it, and shows that under derivative-sector uncertainty the optimally robust derivative-aware relaxation discards the local derivative.

limitations: Global continuously differentiable derivative-sector bounds and existence of a root are assumed.
Exact arithmetic and absolute root error are analyzed; residuals and floating-point effects are not.
The derivative-aware minimax class is memoryless multiplicative relaxation based only on the current derivative and known sector endpoints.
The sufficient strict damping condition gamma<2m/L is prior coverage and is not a novelty claim.
Older relaxed-Newton and nonlinear-equation literature leaves residual historical-equivalence uncertainty.
Independent audit has not been performed.
